text:
ConocoPhillips bounced back 0.84% today to $136.12, recovering from a sharp 3.6% drop on November 18th. The recovery comes as oil prices stabilized: US crude settled at $89.53 per barrel today, up from the lows that accompanied the recent selloff. The stock has clawed back most of its week-over-week losses, suggesting buyers saw the recent decline as overdone given steady energy prices.

The broader energy backdrop remains supportive for a major oil producer. Europe's gas storage concerns heading into winter, potential strains on global electricity grids from data center demand, and the IEA's warning that Middle Eastern supply corridors face persistent uncertainty all point to structural tightness in energy markets—the kind of environment that typically supports oil companies' economics over the medium term.
